full_citation: Sun, S.-G., Z.-H. Huang, Z.-B. Chen, and S.-Q. Huang. 2017. Nectar properties and the role of sunbirds as pollinators of the golden-flowered tea (Camellia petelotii). American Journal of Botany 104:468–476.
exact_evidence_used: Sunbird and honeybee visitation; honeybee visits decline in cloudy/rainy weather; bird exclusion strongly reduces fruit/seed set; nectar volume and sugar composition.
claim_boundary: Demonstrates bird contribution and weather-sensitive bee visitation in this species; not a macroevolutionary colour-selection test.

full_citation: Chai, S.-F., Z.-Y. Chen, J.-M. Tang, M.-L. Wang, R. Zou, and X. Wei. 2019. Breeding system and bird pollination of Camellia pubipetala, a narrowly endemic plant from karst regions of south China. Plant Species Biology 34:141–151.
exact_evidence_used: Fork-tailed sunbird primary; honeybee occasional; open fruit/seed set pollen-limited relative to supplementation.
claim_boundary: Pollinator identity and pollen limitation; not an exclusion effect size or colour-manipulation study.

full_citation: Jiang, H.-D., D.-J. Zeng, H.-Z. Qin, L.-H. Peng, Y.-S. Yang, Z.-Y. Chen, R. Zou, J.-M. Tang, Y.-S. Jiang, Z.-C. Xiong, et al. 2025. Nectar characteristics and pollination ecology of Camellia perpetua in South China. Flora 327:152727.
exact_evidence_used: Bird visitation, fruit set and seed set are higher in winter than summer; winter nectar volume and sucrose proportion are higher.
claim_boundary: Seasonal association/context dependence; not a historical colour-transition test.

full_citation: Kunitake, Y. K., M. Hasegawa, T. Miyashita, and H. Higuchi. 2004. Role of a seasonally specialist bird Zosterops japonica on pollen transfer and reproductive success of Camellia japonica in a temperate area. Plant Species Biology 19:197–201.
exact_evidence_used: Bird-accessible flowers have ~sixfold higher fruit set than flowers excluding birds; Zosterops japonicus is the most effective visitor in the study system.
claim_boundary: Strong bird contribution in this temperate population; not a genus-level pollination syndrome.

full_citation: Abe, H., S. Ueno, T. Takahashi, Y. Tsumura, and M. Hasegawa. 2013. Resilient plant–bird interactions in a volcanic island ecosystem: Pollination of Japanese Camellia mediated by the Japanese White-eye. PLOS ONE 8:e62696.
exact_evidence_used: Volcanic disturbance changes flower density, bird movement/pollen flow and paternal diversity while the bird-mediated pollination interaction persists.
claim_boundary: Disturbance-dependent pollen-flow context; not direct selection on flower colour.

full_citation: Mori, S., Y. Hasegawa, and Y. Moriguchi. 2023. Color strategies of camellias recruiting different pollinators. Phytochemistry 207:113559.
exact_evidence_used: C. japonica and C. rusticana share coarse red colour but differ in UV/fluorescence/sensory strategy and pollinator behaviour; bees prefer C. rusticana in choice tests.
claim_boundary: Supports visible-state aliasing/sensory differences; does not reconstruct macroevolutionary pollinator shifts.

full_citation: Zhang, C., H.-H. Feng, Y.-L. Liu, and S.-Q. Huang. 2024. Lethal effects of tea-oil Camellia on honeybee larvae due to pollen toxicity. Journal of Integrative Plant Biology 66:2313–2316.
exact_evidence_used: Same study reports bird-exclusion cages: fruit set and seed set decline by 56.28% and 27.61%; bagged flowers set no fruit; pollen contains high theasaponin and is toxic to honeybee larvae.
claim_boundary: Contains both bird-exclusion reproductive evidence and pollen-toxicity/anti-bee evidence; do not infer a universal bird syndrome.

full_citation: Li, H.-Y., A.-C. Luo, Y.-J. Hao, F.-Y. Dou, R.-M. Kou, M. C. Orr, C.-D. Zhu, and D.-Y. Huang. 2021. Comparison of the pollination efficiency of Apis cerana with wild bees in oil-seed camellia fields. Basic and Applied Ecology 56:250–258.
exact_evidence_used: Single-visit/behavioural comparisons show wild bees can exceed managed Apis cerana in pollen load, removal/deposition and interplant movement.
claim_boundary: Agricultural-field insect efficiency study; complements but does not negate bird contribution in other contexts.

full_citation: Wickramaratne, M. R. T., and S. I. Vitarana. 1985. Insect pollination of tea (Camellia sinensis L.) in Sri Lanka. Tropical Agriculture 62:243–247.
exact_evidence_used: Diptera are most numerous and efficient in the seed garden; bees are effective but seasonal and less numerous.
claim_boundary: Cultivated tea seed-garden evidence; not a wild-genus syndrome or standardized effect-size estimate.
